tasks.short: Process new books and other materials

steps.what: Process audio-visual materials and computer software
Open a catalog stub when the item identifier is stored

tasks.design: The assistant processes new books, audio-visual materials, and computer software: stamp, cover, and label. {DOCS} opens a catalog stub when the item identifier is already stored. A missing identifier stays blank, and the assistant processes the item without it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each new item was processed with no stub to attach the label to.
tasks.enabler_now: A known identifier can open the stub the label should match.
tasks.still_hard: Stamping, covering, and labeling stay physical.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant stops when the item in hand is not the item named on the stub.
tasks.altitude: Processing stays the week. A known item opens its stub before the label goes on.

reach.task: Decide the processing standard for a new format
reach.learn: Which formats still need a hand label.

evidence.claim: A stored item identifier can open a catalog stub. Stamping, covering, and labeling stay manual.

assumptions: The work starts with a new item and ends when it is stamped, covered, and labeled, with or without a stub.
A stub row has item identifier and title, entered at acquisition. A missing identifier is left blank.
The stub is read, not written, in this task.
unknowns: Which new formats have no identifier yet.
research_questions: How often was the stub missing, so the assistant labeled from the item alone?

already_counted.description: Processing new books is already in the assistant's step.

incremental.description: Correct a stub title after the assistant sees the item does not match.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: new items often have no identifier, so processing is unchanged. High: known items open a stub, and stamping and labeling remain. The range stays under the net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Provide assistance to librarians in maintenance of books, periodicals, and magazines
Provide assistance on newspapers and other audio-visual materials
List gaps in the collections from the stored holdings

tasks.design: The assistant helps librarians maintain collections of books, periodicals, magazines, newspapers, and audio-visual materials. {DOCS} lists titles on the holdings list that have no copy. A blank holdings row is skipped. The assistant still shifts and checks the shelves.
tasks.previous_blocker: Gaps were found by reading the shelf against a paper list.
tasks.enabler_now: Holdings are stored rows, so a missing copy is a comparison.
tasks.still_hard: Shifting the shelf, and judging a worn copy, stay physical.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant tells the librarian when a listed gap is actually a misshelved copy.
tasks.altitude: Shelf help stays. The gap list is something to take to the librarian, not a decision.

reach.learn: Which missing titles the librarian wants seen first.

evidence.claim: Stored holdings can list a title with no copy. Shelf maintenance stays manual.

assumptions: The work starts with a librarian's request and ends when the assistant has shifted the section or handed over a gap list.
A holding row has title identifier and copy count, entered when the item was processed. A blank title is skipped.
The list is read by the librarian. This task does not order a replacement.
unknowns: Which collections the librarian wants checked each week.
research_questions: How often was a listed gap actually on the shelf?

already_counted.description: Helping librarians maintain book and periodical collections is already in the assistant's step.

incremental.description: Correct a copy count after the assistant finds the item on the shelf.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: holdings are incomplete, so the assistant still reads the shelf. High: holdings are complete, and shifting the collection remains. The range stays under the net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review records and identify overdue titles

steps.what: List overdue titles from stored issue cards and microfilm records
Review the list and identify delinquent borrowers
Set aside the overdue materials named on the list

tasks.design: The assistant reviews issue cards and microfilm records. {DOCS} lists titles whose stored due date is before today. The assistant identifies which borrowers are delinquent and sets the materials aside. A missing due date stays off the list.
tasks.previous_blocker: The assistant read every issue card to find the overdue ones.
tasks.enabler_now: The due date is a field, so the overdue list is a date comparison.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding that a borrower is delinquent, and pulling the item, stay with the assistant.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant leaves a borrower off the delinquent list when the card shows a renewal the date missed.

ambition.what: Overdue titles are listed each week, and the assistant still names who is delinquent.

tasks.altitude: The card reading shrinks. Naming a delinquent borrower stays the assistant's decision.

reach.task: Decide the follow-up on a delinquent borrower
reach.learn: Which overdue cases the librarian wants referred.

evidence.claim: A stored due date can list overdue titles. A missing date is left off the list.
Naming a borrower as delinquent is the assistant's judgement. The list does not decide it, and the design does not score patrons.

assumptions: The work starts with issue records and ends when the assistant has identified borrowers and set materials aside, or has stopped.
An issue row has item identifier, borrower identifier, and due date, entered at lending. A microfilm index row has the same fields where the library still uses it. A blank due date is excluded.
No notice is sent in this task. Identification is not a machine label.
unknowns: How the library defines a delinquent borrower beyond a passed due date.
research_questions: How often did the assistant reject a listed title because of a renewal?

already_counted.description: Reviewing the overdue list and identifying borrowers is already in the assistant's step.

incremental.description: Correct a due date the assistant finds renewed or wrong.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: due dates are incomplete, so the assistant still reads the cards. High: dates are complete, and the assistant still identifies borrowers and sets items aside. The range stays under the net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Send overdue notices and accept payments

steps.what: Draft overdue notices for the books from stored fields
Review the overdue notice before it is sent
Accept fine payments for overdue books

tasks.design: The assistant sends notices for overdue books and accepts fine payments. {DOCS} drafts the notice from the stored title, due date, and amount. The assistant reviews it, and {EMAIL} sends only that accepted version. Taking the payment stays at the desk. A missing amount or address stays blank and nothing is sent.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each notice was retyped, and the payment was a separate counter act.
tasks.enabler_now: Title, date, amount, and address are fields, so the notice can be filled and stopped when one is blank.
tasks.still_hard: Taking cash or a card, and judging a dispute at the desk, stay with the assistant.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant will not send a notice, or take a payment, that does not match the book in the record.
tasks.altitude: Payments stay at the desk. A notice leaves only in the text the assistant accepted.

reach.task: Decide a fine the patron disputes
reach.learn: Which disputes the desk must not settle.

evidence.claim: Stored title, date, amount, and address can fill a notice. A missing field stops the send.
An overdue notice names a patron. The assistant accepts that text before it is sent. Taking payment is not automated.

assumptions: The work starts from an overdue row or a patron at the desk and ends with a sent notice, a taken payment, or a stop.
An overdue row has patron identifier, book identifier, due date, amount, and address, entered at lending or registration. A blank amount or address is not invented.
The send uses the notice accepted in the review. Cash handling is not part of that send. No existing scheduled notice is counted as the assistant's time.
unknowns: Whether notices go by post, by mail, or both.
research_questions: How many notices stopped on a blank address, and how many payments were refused?

already_counted.description: Accepting fine payments at the desk is already in the assistant's step.

incremental.description: Correct an amount on a notice the assistant has not yet accepted.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: addresses and amounts are often blank, so notices stay manual and payments are unchanged. High: complete notices are sent after review, and taking the payment remains. The range stays under the net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The assistant still meets patrons, shelves items, and handles cash. A record, notice, invoice, or order is written or sent only after the assistant accepts that version.
reach: A librarian receives the question the assistant could not answer from the desk.
A finance colleague receives only an invoice the assistant has accepted.
skills_to_grow: Stop when a required field is blank.
Accept or refuse the exact version before a send or a write.
Keep shelving, cash, and patron conversations in their own hands.
role.ambitious_version: Every item on loan has a location and a due date the desk can trust, and the assistant still decides the exception.
